glance_takeaway: This is a post-incident report on INC-1194, a June 24 SEV-1 partial API outage lasting 4h17m. Its main message is that there was no single root cause: a rewritten search query combined with two latent weaknesses (vacuum debt from a bulk backfill and jitterless client retries) to turn a one-endpoint regression into a platform-wide partial outage - remove any leg and it's just a degradation. A reader also immediately gets the damage (peak 31.2% API errors, 2,312 orgs / 24.4% affected, ~$41,300 SLA credits, no data lost), that 68 minutes of detection/diagnosis lag came from alerting on error rate rather than latency, that rollback was impossible so a feature flag at 17:05 stopped it, and that three P0 remediation items land in Q3 2026.

F1.note: Subtitle + 'How bad it was' table: 'SEV-1 · 2026-06-24 14:02–18:19 UTC (4 h 17 m)' and '257 min'.

F2.note: Table: '19.1% average across the window; peak 31.2% at 15:47'; '≈362,000 of ≈1.9 M requests'.

F3.note: Table: 'p50 85 ms → 2.9 s; p99 420 ms → 28.4 s'; callout clarifies latency covers completed requests and 30s timeouts surfaced as 504s counted as errors.

F4.note: Table rows: 2,312 orgs (24.4% of 9,480), ≈$41,300 across 216 enterprise contracts, data loss None, 37,400 webhooks replayed by 19:05.

F5.note: Cause 1: PR #8841, leading-wildcard LIKE + org scoping moved to app side, seq scan of 274M-row invoices table, 0.4 ms → 24–31 s. Omits the EXPLAIN cost (8.44 → ≈6.2M) and ~312.3M tuples/scan figures, but the fact's meaning lands correctly.

F6.note: 'the canary table holds ~2 M rows; the same scan there takes ~180 ms, under every alert threshold' + timeline 'Canary was green'.

F7.note: Cause 2: June 22 tax_region backfill, 38.1 M dead tuples, 12.2% bloat, heap 190→213 GB, autovacuum threshold ≈54.9 M not crossed (and why the default is sized wrong for big tables).

F8.note: 'pushed scan times from an estimated ~26 s (bloat-free) to the observed 24–31 s — straddling the 30-second statement timeout. About 57% of search queries were killed... a killed query still held its database connection for the full 30 seconds.'

F9.note: Gloss names the 80-connection pgbouncer pool and its four sharers; '≈5.6/s: demand of 160+ concurrent connections against a pool of 80. Saturation at 15:12'; 'client wait queue peaked at 1,437 at 15:58'; blast-radius framing explicit.

F10.note: 'fixed 1-second interval, 3 attempts, no jitter, no budget... 3,200 rpm baseline to 15,020 rpm at peak — 4.7×... zero extra successes... nearly two hours'; pool bump to 200 at 16:20 backfired, reverted 16:31.

F11.note: Timeline row 14:20–15:10 (50 minutes, packet-loss advisory anchor) + 'Why diagnosis took 68 minutes' covers the 14:05 advisory, 504s resembling network timeouts, deploy markers broken since June 10, and 68 min from 14:11 to 15:19.

F12.note: 'migration 0412, which dropped idx_invoices_org_number... rolling back the code would restore the old query with no index to serve it... Rebuilding the index on 274 M rows takes ~6 hours (started at 16:05... finished at 21:48, after incident close)'.

F13.note: 'invoice_search_contains' to 0% at 17:05 after staging verification of exact-match fallback on the untouched unique index; flip took 90 s; errors below 3% by 17:15 (timeline); exact-match-only until re-enable June 26. Only the 16:35 staging timestamp is omitted.

F14.note: Timeline: manual VACUUM 17:12–17:50 removing 38.1 M dead tuples and refreshing statistics; 17:53 all endpoint groups within SLO; 18:19 closed after 26 minutes stable.

F15.note: 'Why diagnosis took 68 minutes': only alert was error-rate (gateway 5xx > 2%, fired 14:11), no latency SLO for invoicing though p99 exploded at 14:07, dashboards sampled 1/100 (~0.7 samples/min), broken deploy marker hid the 14:02 deploy.

F16.note: 'What we're changing' table: 9 items (3 P0/3 P1/3 P2) with named owners and quarters; the three Q3-2026 P0s (Priya N. latency SLO alerts, Marcus T. pgbouncer saturation + isolation, Dana K. backoff/jitter/budgets) and the P1s (autovacuum tuning, migration-reversibility policy, CI plan checks) all match.

strengths: Complete and faithful: all 16 ground-truth facts land, with exact figures (57% kill rate, 1,437 cl_waiting peak, 4.7x retry multiplier, 54.9M autovacuum threshold) and no overselling.
The above-the-fold summary is exceptional: all four required takeaways are stated in the first two paragraphs, so even a 10-second glance delivers the causal thesis.
Causal structure is explicit, not flattened: 'a trigger and two amplifiers' framing, a numbered end-to-end chain, and remove-one-leg counterfactuals for each leg.
Audience fit: every DB mechanism (B-tree vs leading wildcard, dead tuples/autovacuum, pgbouncer pooling, covering index) gets a one-line gloss, exactly as the brief requires.
Measurement caveats are surfaced in a dedicated 'Reading the numbers' callout; blameless tone preserved throughout ('fixing the instruments, not second-guessing the people').
weaknesses: Almost no visual encoding: the error-rate trajectory, the 4h17m time budget, and the three-legged causal structure are all narrated or tabulated, never diagrammed or charted - the visual channel is essentially unused.
No table of contents or anchor links on a very long single page; re-finding a specific number means scrolling and scanning headers.
At ~2,500 words the page strains the brief's 'in a few minutes' reading goal; the deep detail (EXPLAIN mechanics, pool arithmetic) is mixed inline rather than progressively disclosed.
A few evidentiary sub-figures are dropped (EXPLAIN cost 8.44 to ~6.2M, ~312.3M tuples read per scan, 16:35 staging-verification time), slightly weakening the quantitative backing for Cause 1.
evaluator_notes: Judged blind per rubric v1. Glance scored solely from the recorded glance_takeaway: T1 and T3 land fully, T2 substantially (misses the 1/100 sampling and hidden deploy marker mechanics), T4 partially (count/quarter/blameless visible, fix content not). Accuracy is mechanical: 16 conveyed, 0 distorted/contradicted = 10.0; the page is an unusually faithful rendering of the source. Depth held to 8.0 rather than higher because length works against the stated few-minute goal. Visual craft 6.0: what little visual design exists (typography, tabular-nums timeline, accent-colored thesis, dark mode) is clean and honest, but the material's causal and temporal structure begged for at least one diagram and got none. Overall = 0.35*10.0 + 0.30*8.5 + 0.15*8.0 + 0.10*7.0 + 0.10*6.0 = 8.6 (rounded from 8.55).
